header:
Date: 2027-02-16
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Hannah Lee (Redwood Support) -- Tom Avery (Aurelia VP Eng), Priya Singh (Aurelia Lead SRE), Ben Clarke (Aurelia Infra), Renee Caldwell (Aurelia Security PM)
Files shared: link: /redwood/poc/aur-synthetic-playbook.xlsx, link: /redwood/security/soc2-scoping.pdf
summary: Weekly pilot sync. Main topics: telemetry spike last week correlated with kernel upgrade on private nodes, routing fallback efficacy, MTU/egress shaping causing packet drops on certain on-prem NICs, and plan for controlled rollback and a synthetic traffic replay. Action items assigned for kernel rollback test, traffic sample delivery, and maintenance window planning. Decided on temporary canary to route 10% traffic to older model variant while rollback is validated.
topics: MTU / egress shaping impact on KV cache warm-up
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. we'll keep this tight—55 minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Tom Avery: Tom here, Priya, Ben and Renee are on as well.
[00:00:14] Maya Chen: great. Luis, can you give a 2-minute recap of what we observed after the kernel upgrade last thursday?
[00:00:21] Luis Ortega: yeah so um, we pushed the newer kernel + quantized-kernel patch to the private canary nodes. immediately some of the synthetic runs showed a p99 tail increase, from like 420ms to 980ms for the 3B quantized variant. looks like an nvlink/driver interaction with our optimized attention kernel, maybe context-switching amplification. not consistent across regions — only on the on-prem rack with Broadcom NICs.
[00:00:45] Priya Singh: we noticed correlated retransmits on the socket layer and some MTU blackholing, 1500 vs 9000 mismatch on one of the switches. that caused a couple of tcp retransmits that pushed the request to fallback, which then warmed a different model and caused duplicate KV cache populates. weird warm-up pattern.
[00:01:05] Ben Clarke: we had intermittent CPU steal on the host too, from the backup job that spikes every 04:00 UTC—shouldn't have happened but it did. combined with the packet drops, latency spiked.
[00:01:16] Luis Ortega: yeah and on the Redwood side the routing policy triggered fallback to a smaller quantized model variant, which is good for availability but users saw output variation and a few timeouts.
[00:01:25] Maya Chen: ok, so two parallel threads: kernel-driver interaction and network MTU/egress shaping. what's the pragmatic rollback plan?
[00:01:34] Luis Ortega: pragmatic is rollback the kernel on canary, run a controlled replay, compare the p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. if rollback reduces tail we do a staged rollback, otherwise we push a driver patch. we should capture perf counters too.
[00:01:46] Tom Avery: can we do that in staging first? we can't risk prod instability.
[00:01:49] Luis Ortega: absolutely, plan is staging then small canary in on-prem rack.
[00:01:52] Priya Singh: also we need to address the MTU mismatch, our switches defaulted to 1500 after a recent maintenance. that'll be a separate on-prem change but low risk.
[00:02:00] Maya Chen: good. Samir, any customer impact telemetry you can share?
[00:02:04] Samir Patel: yeah we saw a 3% error-rate uptick for the POC cluster during the window, and anomalies in token rates where a small subset of requests doubled token cost because of duplicate prefix caching from fallback. we've summarized in the sheet linked earlier.
[00:02:16] Priya Singh: about fallback routing — how quickly can Redwood tune the threshold that triggers model fallback? the current policy seems aggressive.
[00:02:24] Luis Ortega: we can tune threshold and also add hysteresis. right now it reacts on p95 breaches over 3-minute windows; we can extend to 10 minutes with dampening so transient spikes won't flip the route. that's a quick config change.
[00:02:36] Maya Chen: and the canary plan for routing?
[00:02:38] Luis Ortega: propose 10% traffic to rollback-v0 variant for 24 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99 and model output drift using existing eval hooks. if stable, ramp 10→50→100. otherwise revert.
[00:02:50] Tom Avery: that sounds reasonable. can you also log per-request routing decision? we need to map events back to customer traces.
[00:02:55] Hannah Lee: we can add a routing decision header and trace id so you can join it with your observability. we'll supply the join keys.
[00:03:02] Priya Singh: about the MTU fix — we can schedule a low-impact maintenance window, but we need Redwood to re-run the synthetic replay after that so we can isolate variables.
[00:03:10] Maya Chen: agreed. next, kernel telemetry: what counters do we need to capture?
[00:03:14] Luis Ortega: cpu context switches, nvlink errors, driver dmesg tail, kernel skb drop counts, and the runtime's async IO queue depth. also token-level timings from the runtime to separate network vs compute.
[00:03:26] Ben Clarke: we can forward dmesg and perf counters to your agent; we'll redact sensitive hostnames.
[00:03:30] Maya Chen: perfect. about the KV cache warm-up duplication — can you explain that sequence again?
[00:03:35] Luis Ortega: sure. a request hits node A which, because of transient packet loss, falls back to smaller model on node B. node B doesn't have the KV cache warmed so it issues the full prompt, causing duplicate prefixes stored and extra token generation. that increased token costs and latency. We can mitigate with prefix-hinting and a short-lived shared cache or by lowering fallback sensitivity.
[00:03:55] Priya Singh: prefix-hinting would need a secure channel to pass small caches between nodes — is that supported?
[00:03:59] Luis Ortega: we have a lightweight prefix-hint proto — it's off by default for security reasons but can be enabled within the VPC with mutual TLS. we'd need your sign-off.
[00:04:08] Renee Caldwell: security caveat — any cross-node cache sharing in the VPC must be encrypted and logged. also need an audit trail for cache access.
[00:04:15] Maya Chen: understoood — Redwood's prefix-hint over mTLS includes audit headers and we'll tie to KMS-managed keys if you enable it. we'll share design doc.
[00:04:22] Samir Patel: quick note on the user-visible quality delta: 6 of 4000 user requests in the sample had semantically different responses after the fallback. not huge but enough to be noticed in a prod-facing flow.
[00:04:34] Tom Avery: unacceptable for our main cohort. We need to keep fallback to degrade gracefully without changing semantics when possible.
[00:04:40] Luis Ortega: we can bias fallback routing to prefer same-model family variants and avoid smaller model class unless latency risk is extreme. also we can add a soft-fail that retries once before switching model.
[00:04:52] Maya Chen: ok, do we have enough to proceed with kernel rollback test and MTU maintenance?
[00:04:56] Priya Singh: yes. we'll set the maintenance window for Feb 22 UTC off-peak.
[00:05:00] Tom Avery: Luis, what's the expected telemetry turnaround after you run rollback?
[00:05:04] Luis Ortega: initial results within 24 hours; we'll push a short report with numbers and traces.
[00:05:08] Maya Chen: can you also include the synthetic replay script and the exact request set you used so it's reproducible?
[00:05:12] Luis Ortega: yes. we'll push the script to the shared folder and include CLI flags for token size and concurrency.
[00:05:20] Priya Singh: about security docs — Renee, you'll review SOC2 scoping?
[00:05:24] Renee Caldwell: yes, I'll review and get back by Feb 24.
[00:05:27] Maya Chen: great. closing questions?
[00:05:30] Ben Clarke: one ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook for emergency forced-fallback and rollback steps?
[00:05:35] Maya Chen: yes, we have a playbook. we'll tailor a short 'on-call' one-page runbook for your team and share it.
[00:05:41] Samir Patel: I'll also add a section in the sheet with 'observed at' timestamps to help correlate.
[00:05:45] Tom Avery: thanks everyone. let's reconvene after the rollback validation — propose a 30-minute sync on Feb 21 if we have interim results.
[00:05:52] Maya Chen: sounds good. thanks all.
[00:05:55] (call ends)
notes: Redwood to prioritize rollback test before pushing any further kernel patches
Customer to provide traffic samples and schedule MTU maintenance
Security signoff on prefix-hint needed for enabling cache sharing
